rules.statement: Give helper methods that only read text a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` parameter instead of `string`, so callers can pass slices without allocating; keep `string` on public contract types such as request properties.
rules.why: A `string` converts to `ReadOnlySpan<char>` implicitly, so a span parameter still accepts every existing caller and also takes slices with no allocation.
rules.check: Look for new or changed methods that take a `string` they only read (hashing, encoding, comparing) when a `ReadOnlySpan<char>` would work.

rules.statement: Put a setting that a protocol registers per client (for example the OIDC `id_token_signed_response_alg` ID-token signing algorithm) on the per-client registration model, not on a process-wide .NET options class.
rules.why: OIDC registers these values per client, and the protocol client must not bind process-wide configuration.
rules.check: Look for per-client protocol settings added to an `IOptions<T>` options class rather than to the client registration/settings type.

rules.statement: Use the existing public constant for a well-known protocol value (for example `AlgorithmCodes.DigitalSignature.None` for the JOSE `none` algorithm) instead of declaring a private string constant or literal.
rules.why: A shared public constant already exists and other code uses it; duplicating the literal adds a second source of truth.
rules.check: Look for private `const string` fields or inline literals such as "none" or algorithm names that duplicate a public constant already in the codebase.

rules.statement: When the same hash or crypto operation of a fixed output size runs several times in a row, allocate the output buffer once in the caller and pass it in as a `Span<byte>`, instead of letting each call allocate its own.
rules.why: Allocating once and reusing the buffer for all the consecutive hashes (for example `at_hash`, `c_hash`, `s_hash`) avoids allocating on every call, and an earlier version that allocated per call was a regression.
rules.check: Look for loops or consecutive calls to a hashing helper that allocates or stackallocs its output each time, where the size is the same for every call and a buffer could be passed in.

rules.statement: For temporary encoding buffers, use `stackalloc` up to a small fixed limit (for example 256 bytes) and rent from a pool for anything longer, instead of allocating on the heap.
rules.why: This keeps hot paths such as token hash computation and verification free of heap allocations.
rules.check: Look for `new byte[]` or `Encoding.GetBytes(string)` that returns an array for a short-lived buffer, where a stackalloc buffer with a rented fallback would work.
